Subject: Mutual action plan: data handling & deployment mode decisions

Hi Soojin / Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed on the call, we've drafted a first-pass mutual action plan (attached) so our security and infra teams can align on deployment mode and PII/retention guarantees during evaluation. High-level asks from Acme:

- Clarify which data types (logs, request payloads, embeddings) may leave our VPC under Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Confirm retention windows for request logs and KV caches; we need options to cap at 30/90/365 days.
- Describe PII handling: redaction, encryption-at-rest, and whether Redwood will perform automatic masking before any telemetry leaves our environment.
- For on-prem subset: we need a checklist for an air-gapped install and a clear owner at Redwood.

Attached: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx with milestones. Can you propose owners and a target close timeline (we're aiming for a decision by end of Q1).

Best,
Alice Wong
Senior InfoSec Program Manager
Acme Financials

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks for the MAP draft, I reviewed and added a couple of milestone rows (shared as a Drive link in my notes). Quick answers and proposed owners below; I'll consolidate into a formal MAP snapshot and share before Friday's checkpoint.

Proposed owners (first pass):
- Deployment mode & SCAR (service-capability routing): Soojin Lee (Redwood Sales/Platform) — own customer-facing decisions and rollout schedule.
- Security/compliance & PII policy: Rishi Malhotra (Redwood Security) — own answers re: masking/encryption/SOC2 artifacts.
- Private/on-prem checklist: Priyom Das (Redwood Private Eng) — lead on air-gap requirements and install plan.

Quick responses:
- Hosted API: telemetry (non-PII) may be aggregated for platform health; any PII must be excluded by customer config or redaction rules.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): data isolation provides tenant-level separation; retention windows configurable via our console; default logging retention is 90 days.
- Private (VPC/On-prem): data does not leave customer network; we provide installers and an ops-runbook, but some telemetry for billing/health is optional and can be disabled.

Next steps: can we confirm a 60-minute sync on Thu 1/14 to walk Rishi through the PII examples and for Priyom to capture on-prem constraints? I've tentatively put Thu 1/14 11:00am PT on the calendar (invite to follow).

Thanks — I'll follow up with the consolidated MAP and action-item table.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: technical checklist for Acme on-prem subset

Soojin / Priyom — notes from my read of ACME_MAP_v1 and follow-ups we should be ready with during the Thu sync: 

1) On-prem/air-gapped checklist (Priyom owner):
   - Installer bundle + SHA256 signatures (we provide signed tarball).
   - KMS integration: HSM/KMS options documented; we support customer-managed keys for model artifacts and logs.
   - Network egress: explicit list of endpoints; option to disable telemetry/heartbeat and ship logs via customer proxy.

2) Data retention & PII handling (Rishi owner):
   - Default request logging retention: 90 days, configurable via console (30/90/365 presets).
   - KV cache eviction: customer-configurable TTL; recommend <7 days for PII-sensitive workloads.
   - PII detection: we have a regex-heuristic and ML-backed redaction pipeline, BUT automatic redaction is opt-in for hosted flows — for Dedicated/Private we can enable on-request.

3) Audit evidence & SOC2 artifacts (Rishi + Soojin):
   - Provide SOC2 summary and recent cert.
   - Logs export: we can provide daily exports to S3 with lifecycle rules.

4) Risk items to call out on call:
   - For model telemetry (gradients/weights): confirm no model parameters are retained; only token-level metadata.
   - Embedding storage: embeddings persisted only if customer enables; default is in-memory TTL limited.

I'll prepare a one-pager (redwood-data-handling-checklist.pdf) for the call. Priyom — can you prepare the installer dependency matrix and a rough timeline for on-prem delivery?

—Rishi
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-handling-checklist.pdf (PDF - 28kb)

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: data handling & deployment mode decisions

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the checklist, team. A couple of clarifications from Acme Sec: 

- On-prem requirement: we will require an on-prem install for our transaction-PII processing path (approx 15% of traffic). Dedicated/Hosted can be used for anonymized/aggregate workflows.
- Retention: for transaction logs we need a hard cap of 90 days. For audit logs (access, admin) we require 7 years (can be exported off-platform).
- PII masking: we need proof-of-redaction for evaluation — can Redwood run a redaction job on a small sample dataset and provide the before/after as part of the eval?

Also, Priyom — please include constraints for PCI-similar environments (we don't expect full PCI compliance, but we need clear binding points for network isolation and no-telemetry mode).

Proposed next steps for Thu sync: walk through the on-prem installer checklist and agree owners and delivery dates. If we can get the sample redaction run by Wed 1/20 that would be very helpful for our legal review.

Best,
Alice Wong
Senior InfoSec Program Manager
Acme Financials

- Retention: agreed hard cap for transaction logs = 90 days (Redwood default 90d, configurable). Audit logs: exportable to S3 for 7-year retention — Rishi will provide export runbook.
- PII redaction: Redwood will run a sample redaction job (anonymized output + redaction report) for Acme datasets in staging.

Next meeting: Thu 2027-01-21 11:00am PT (60m) — link and calendar invite to follow.
